name: Central-bank balance sheet / system liquidity contract

objectSeparation.FED_ASSET_STOCK: SOMA securities and other Reserve Bank assets; balance-sheet stock, not equivalent to current system liquidity.
objectSeparation.RESERVE_BALANCES: Depository-institution balances at Federal Reserve Banks; core banking-system reserve quantity.
objectSeparation.TGA: U.S. Treasury General Account, a non-reserve Fed liability whose changes can mechanically shift reserves absent offsetting asset changes.
objectSeparation.ON_RRP: Overnight reverse-repo balances; a separate Fed liability/liquidity-absorption channel.
objectSeparation.CURRENCY: Currency in circulation; non-reserve liability that can reduce reserve supply as it grows absent offsetting asset changes.
objectSeparation.ADMINISTERED_RATES: IORB/ON-RRP/SRF policy-implementation prices; not balance-sheet quantities.
objectSeparation.MONEY_MARKET_STRESS: EFFR-IORB/repo-rate/SRF usage and related signals of reserve scarcity/distribution.

balanceSheetIdentity.principle: Assets = liabilities + capital. Reserve balances are residual to asset-side and non-reserve-liability movements, not a direct synonym for total assets.
balanceSheetIdentity.implication: A decline in Fed assets can coexist with temporarily stable/rising reserves if TGA/ON-RRP/other liabilities move in the offsetting direction; likewise assets can be stable while reserves fall as TGA or currency rises.

ampleReservesFramework.officialFramework: Federal Reserve currently implements policy in an ample-reserves regime, relying primarily on administered rates rather than active fine-tuning of reserve quantity.
ampleReservesFramework.thresholdGuard: Ample is a range, not a fixed reserve-balance number; reserve demand changes with banking/payment/regulatory conditions.

systemLiquidity.descriptiveCandidate: reserveBalances + selected ON_RRP balances only under an explicitly frozen accounting purpose
systemLiquidity.guard: No universal 'net liquidity = Fed assets - TGA - ONRRP' alpha formula without precise liability coverage, accounting identity and mechanism. Popular net-liquidity formulas are heuristic and can omit currency/other liabilities and reserve-demand effects.
systemLiquidity.tgaMechanics: A TGA drawdown can mechanically raise reserves/system liquidity; a TGA rebuild can drain reserves, absent offsets.
systemLiquidity.onRrpMechanics: ON RRP can absorb/release liquidity across counterparties and can shrink while reserves remain ample; its level is regime-dependent.
